summary:
Most of the Claude work this week went into making phillipsben.com dashboard refresh reliable. The daily job that updates this page runs on a local model, and it was tripping over the fiddly mechanical steps — so the fix was to hand it a real orchestrator: deterministic code does the fetching, schema assembly, validation, and a freshness check, and the model only writes the short narrative bits you're reading.

On the hermes-agent side, that meant tracing a deploy end-to-end: confirming the webhook rebuild was healthy, then proving only one tile had actually refreshed and finding why. A music service token sitting with the wrong file permissions turned out to be a self-inflicted snag from debugging, now fixed.

The throughline lately is treating an agent like any other production system — make the happy path boring, make failures loud, and stop trusting a "looks done" report when a one-line check can confirm it.

highlights.oneLiner: Implemented a deterministic dashboard refresh orchestrator and fixed pop-os memory snapshot paths.
